CLARKE OUTDOOR SPRAYING COMPANY, Inc.
MOSQUITO CONTROL - AQUATIC WEED CONTROL
INSPECTION . LARVICIDING . FOGGING . MISTING
200 HAYES AVENUE
LA GRANGE, ILLINOIS 60525
September 23, 1971
Mr. Dan Tankersley Monticello Street Winnamac, Indiana 46996
Dear Mr. Tankersley:
This is to confirm our conversation regarding a possible solution for the wild marijuana crop within Pulaski county.
For the last two summers our company has used a new technique to treat 600 acres of scattered marijuana growth on Metropolitan Sanitary District grounds southwest of Chicago.
This method utilizes dry 2,4-D granules which are applied in mid May, just as the new marijuana plants emerge. The 2,4-D is released by the granules at ground level wher it is rapidly picked up by the new plants. The plants are destroyed by the time they are a foot high.
This technique has the following advantages:
1. The marijuana is eliminated early in the season before a picking problem develops.
2. Grass is unaffected by the 2,4-D and moves in rapidly to take over areas vacated by the marijuana plants.
3. No browning out of vegetation develops as with the late summer programs.
4. The dry granules don't pose a spray drift or wildlife problem.
This treatment should be repeated annually over a several year period until the marijuana seeds are exhausted and other plant growth has taken over. Dr. Ellery L. Knake, Professor of Agronomy at the University of Illinois is familiar with this technique.
Mr. James Highland, grounds superentendent at the Southwest treatment plant, Metropolitan Sanitary District, A.C. 312+242-3144 ext. 437 would be glad to discuss the results of the Districts marijuana eradication program with you.
